blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
blocks.md: Full fine-tuning of an agent policy updates and stores a complete replica of every base parameter, requiring the training system to allocate memory for base weights, gradients, and optimizer state across the entire model. For an adaptive-moment optimizer under mixed precision, that state is a higher-precision master copy of each weight plus two running moments, so each trained parameter carries several times the bytes of its weight. Training a second specialized agent role, such as a diagnostic planner or an execution monitor, duplicates that resource footprint in full.

questions.q: The section **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.
Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.
A corpus with one static tool signature lets the policy memorize argument keys, so augmentation transforms the whole decision context coherently and robustness is measured on held-out schemas.
A training example reconstructs each selected response's input exactly as the model received it, truncations and redactions included, under a recorded tokenizer and template configuration.
